about.Markdown basics: Headings, bold, lists, links and to-dos: what every Markdown app reads the same way.
about.More Markdown: Tables, pictures, footnotes, maths, callouts and diagrams.
about.Lines that do more: Tags, choices, counters, sums, blanks for the AI and comments: lines whose words the note works with.
about.Links and places: Another note, the bookmark you left, and a place on a map.
about.Boards and to-dos: Due days and people on a to-do, names for items, and boards made of them.
about.Tickets and queries: Notes as tickets, and queries that list, count and lay out what matches in every note.
about.Marks and effects: Highlights, spoilers, asides and the five effects, from the Marks plugin.

lessons.title: A title
lessons.teach: A note usually starts with its name. One # and a space makes that line the title, and it is what the note is called in your list.
lessons.task: Give a note a title of your own.
lessons.hint: Start the line with # and a space, then the words.

lessons.title: A heading
lessons.teach: More hashes, smaller heading: ## for a part of the note, ### for a part of that. It is how a long note gets somewhere to look.
lessons.task: Write a heading for part of a note.
lessons.hint: Two hashes and a space: ## The budget.

lessons.title: Bold
lessons.teach: Two stars either side of some words make them bold. The stars themselves go once the line is written.
lessons.task: Write a line with something bold in it.
lessons.hint: Two stars, the words, two stars: **like this**.

lessons.title: Italic
lessons.teach: One underscore either side leans the words over. It is quieter than bold: an aside, a name, a word said with a shrug.
lessons.example: we could take the coast road _if the weather holds_
lessons.task: Write a line with something in italics.
lessons.hint: An underscore either side: _like this_.

lessons.title: Bold and italic
lessons.teach: Three stars either side make words bold and italic at once. Keep it for the one thing that must not be missed.
lessons.task: Make a word or two bold and italic at once.
lessons.hint: Three stars either side: ***like this***.

lessons.title: Struck through
lessons.teach: Two squiggles either side cross the words out. Good for a plan that changed, where you still want to see what it was.
lessons.example: we are going ~~on Thursday~~ on Friday
lessons.task: Cross some words out.
lessons.hint: Two squiggles either side: ~~like this~~.

lessons.title: Code
lessons.teach: A backtick either side sets the words in the typewriter face and leaves them exactly as you typed them: a command, a filename, a password to read out.
lessons.task: Write a line with a bit of code in it.
lessons.hint: A backtick either side: `like this`. The key is usually under Escape.

lessons.title: A link
lessons.teach: The words people read go in square brackets, and where they point goes in round ones after it. The note shows the words, not the address.
lessons.example: [Ghost.md](https://attack.fm/glyph) is the app this is in
lessons.task: Write a link of your own.
lessons.hint: Words in square brackets, then the address in round ones: [words](https://example.com).

lessons.title: A list
lessons.teach: A dash and a space starts a list, one line each. Press Enter and the next line is a bullet too.
lessons.task: Write a list of two or three things.
lessons.hint: Start each line with a dash and a space.

lessons.title: In order
lessons.teach: A number, a dot and a space when the order is the point: steps to follow, one after another.
lessons.example:
1. Unplug it
2. Wait a minute
3. Plug it back in
lessons.task: Write two steps in order.
lessons.hint: Start the line with 1. and a space; the next one with 2.

lessons.title: A to-do
lessons.teach: A dash, then a box: - [ ] and the thing to do. Tap the box in a note to tick it off, or type an x between the brackets.
lessons.example:
- [ ] Book the cabin
- [x] Pick a date
lessons.task: Write something you have to do.
lessons.praise: That is a to-do, and its box is real: tap it in a note.
lessons.hint: A dash, a space, then [ ] with a space between the brackets.

lessons.title: A quote
lessons.teach: A > and a space sets a line apart: somebody else’s words, or something you want to stand away from the rest.
lessons.example: > The deposit comes back in full.
lessons.task: Quote a line.
lessons.hint: Start the line with > and a space.

lessons.title: A dividing line
lessons.teach: Three dashes on a line of their own draw a line across the note: one thing ends, another starts.
lessons.task: Put a line between two parts of a note.
lessons.hint: Three dashes alone on a line: ---

lessons.title: A block of code
lessons.teach: Three backticks above and below a few lines keeps every one of them exactly as typed, and colors the code if you say what it is after the first three.
lessons.task: Write a block with a line or two of code in it.
lessons.praise: A block, kept exactly as typed.
lessons.hint: Three backticks on their own line, your code, then three more.

lessons.title: A table
lessons.teach: Pipes between the cells, and a row of dashes under the first row. In a note the table is drawn as a table; a tap on it opens its pipes to change it, and it is drawn again when you leave it.
lessons.task: Make a table with a row or two in it.
lessons.hint: A row of cells between pipes, then | --- | --- | under it, then the rest of the rows.

lessons.title: A picture
lessons.teach: An exclamation mark, what the picture shows in square brackets, and where it is in round ones. In a note you seldom type it: paste a picture, or press and hold and choose Add image, and the line is written for you.
lessons.task: Write the line for a picture.
lessons.hint: An exclamation mark, then [what it shows], then (where it is).

lessons.title: A video
lessons.teach: A picture of the film’s first frame, linked to the film itself. You never type it: on Android, the + beside an empty line writes it when you choose A video. The film stays on the phone it was added on; everywhere else the still shows.
lessons.task: Write a video’s line, as the + would.
lessons.hint: A picture’s line inside a link’s square brackets, then (video/ and the file’s name).

lessons.title: Raised
lessons.teach: A caret either side lifts part of a word above the line: the 2nd of June, a power in a sum.
lessons.task: Raise part of a word.
lessons.hint: A caret either side of the part to lift: 2^nd^.

lessons.title: Lowered
lessons.teach: One squiggle either side drops part of a word below the line, the way water is written. Two squiggles cross words out, which is a lesson of its own.
lessons.task: Lower part of a word.
lessons.hint: One squiggle either side: H~2~O.

lessons.title: A footnote
lessons.teach: A caret and a name in square brackets marks the words, and a line that starts with the same mark and a colon says what it is. In a note the mark is raised, and a tap on it shows the small print.
lessons.task: Write a line with a footnote, and the footnote.
lessons.praise: That is a footnote, and a tap reads it.
lessons.hint: A mark like [^sam] after the words, and a line under them that starts [^sam]: and says it.

lessons.title: A definition
lessons.teach: A word on one line, and its meaning on the next, starting with a colon and a space. The colon goes at the start of the meaning’s line, not after the word, which is how Markdown apps know it is a definition; drawn, it is gone and the meaning hangs under the word. It is how a glossary is written.
lessons.example:
Deposit
: what you pay up front
lessons.task: Define a word.
lessons.hint: The word, then on the next line a colon, a space, and what it means.

lessons.title: Maths
lessons.teach: A dollar sign either side makes a formula, drawn as one: a raised power, a fraction, a Greek letter. Two either side, alone on a line, set it in the middle of the page. With the caret on its line you see what you typed, to edit.
lessons.example: the area is $\pi r^2$, and half is $\frac{1}{2}$
lessons.task: Write a formula.
lessons.hint: A dollar sign either side, no space inside them: $x^2$. A fraction is \frac{top}{bottom}.

lessons.title: An emoji
lessons.teach: A name between colons becomes its emoji: :tada: is a party popper. The name comes back while the caret is on the line, and a name Ghost.md does not know stays as it was typed.
lessons.task: Put an emoji in a line by its name.
lessons.hint: A colon either side of the name: :tada:, :rocket:, :coffee:.

lessons.title: A callout
lessons.teach: A quote whose first line is [!NOTE] becomes a box of its own. TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING and CAUTION work the same way.
lessons.example:
> [!NOTE]
> The deposit comes back in full.
lessons.task: Write a callout.
lessons.hint: A quote with the kind on its first line: > [!TIP]

lessons.title: A diagram
lessons.teach: A block of code marked mermaid is drawn as the diagram it describes: boxes, and the arrows between them. Tap a drawn diagram in a note to change its words.
lessons.task: Draw two boxes and an arrow.
lessons.hint: Three backticks and mermaid, then flowchart TD, then a line like A --> B, then three backticks.

lessons.title: A tag
lessons.teach: A hash against a word, with no space between, tags the line: #web. A tag can hold a slash, #work/clients, which apps like Obsidian read as one tag inside another. A hash and a space at the start of a line is a heading instead.
lessons.task: Tag a line.
lessons.hint: A # and the word, with no space between: #web.

lessons.title: A choice
lessons.teach: Round brackets on a list make a choice. One in the group is picked, with an x, and a tap on another picks it and clears the rest. Try it on the one drawn below.
lessons.example:
Where do we stay?
- ( ) Tent
- (x) Cabin
lessons.task: Write a choice with two options.
lessons.praise: That is a choice: tap one below to pick it.
lessons.hint: A dash, a space, then ( ) with a space between the brackets.

lessons.title: A counter
lessons.teach: A count and a goal in square brackets, like [3/8], is a counter. In a note a tap adds one and a hold takes one away, never past the goal.
lessons.task: Count something toward a goal.
lessons.hint: Two numbers with a slash between, in square brackets: [0/8].

lessons.title: A sum
lessons.teach: A line that starts with = and a space shows its answer after it. The answer is never written into the note, so it changes when a number does.
lessons.task: Do a sum.
lessons.hint: An equals sign, a space, then the sum: = 12 * 4.

lessons.title: A blank for the AI
lessons.teach: Curly brackets and a question mark ask a question where its answer belongs. A total, a date or a conversion is worked out at once. Anything else waits for Fill: the model on the phone answers with a dotted line under what it wrote, and something live, like the weather or a rate, is looked up online when you press it, with only the question sent.
lessons.task: Write a blank.
lessons.hint: A curly bracket, a question mark, the question, then a closing bracket: {?which day}.

lessons.title: A hidden line
lessons.teach: A quote whose first character is a bar goes to smoke until the caret is in it: the answer to a riddle, or a code nobody should read over your shoulder.
lessons.task: Hide a line.
lessons.hint: A > and a bar, with no space between, then the line: >| like this.

lessons.title: Progress
lessons.teach: Nothing to type but a heading and its to-dos: the heading counts them, “1 of 2”, and says so when they are all done.
lessons.task: Write a heading with a to-do or two under it.
lessons.hint: A heading, then a line like - [ ] Stove under it.

lessons.title: A comment
lessons.teach: A comment is kept in the note itself: a mark like [^c1] after the words it is about, or ==round them==[^c1], and the thread in a ```comments block at the end - its id, who and when, then the words, with replies indented under it. Comment on the press-and-hold menu, in More and in the bar writes both for you.
lessons.example:
Call the band[^c1]

```comments
c1 me 2026-10-05T09:00:00Z
Which band?
```
lessons.task: Write a line with a comment mark, and its thread in a comments block.
lessons.praise: That is a comment, and its mark opens the thread.
lessons.hint: A mark like [^c1] after the words, then a ```comments block with a line like c1 me 2026-10-05T09:00:00Z and the words under it.

lessons.title: Another note
lessons.teach: Two square brackets either side of a note’s name link to that note. A name with no note yet is drawn dashed, and a tap on it makes the note.
lessons.example: the deposit is in [[The cabin trip]]
lessons.task: Link to a note by its name.
lessons.hint: Two square brackets either side of the name: [[The cabin trip]].

lessons.title: The bookmark
lessons.teach: Two section signs at the end of a line are the note’s bookmark, and the note opens there. A note has one; the bookmark button at the top of a note moves it to the line you are on.
lessons.task: Bookmark a line.
lessons.hint: Two section signs at the very end of the line: §§

lessons.title: A place
lessons.teach: A link to geo: and two numbers, alone on its line, is a place, with its map drawn under it. The + beside an empty line writes one for where you are.
lessons.task: Put a place of your own on a line.
lessons.praise: That is a place, with its map.
lessons.hint: Its name in square brackets, then geo: and the two numbers in round ones: [Home](geo:51.5074,-0.1278).

lessons.title: Fields on a to-do
lessons.teach: A to-do can say when it is due, how much it matters and who it is for, in the signs Obsidian Tasks reads: 📅 and a date, ⏫ for high priority, @ before a name, and [effort:: 3] for anything else. In a note each is a chip: the date says “Tomorrow”, and goes red once it has passed. Tap one to change it, or press and hold a to-do to add one.
lessons.task: Give a to-do a due date, a priority or a person.
lessons.hint: After the words, @ and a name is the quickest: - [ ] Book the cabin @sam. A date is 📅 then 2026-10-03.

lessons.title: A name for an item
lessons.teach: A space, a caret and a name at the very end of a list item names it, so a board or a sentence can point at it. The name is drawn small and faint.
lessons.task: Name an item on a list.
lessons.hint: At the end of the item, a space, a caret and a name with no spaces: ^ship-page.

lessons.title: That item, from the words
lessons.teach: Two square brackets around a hash, a caret and an item’s name point at that item from anywhere in the note. A tap goes to its line.
lessons.example:
the page is waiting on [[#^ask-sam]]

- Ask Sam about the copy ^ask-sam
lessons.task: Point at a named item from a sentence.
lessons.hint: Two square brackets around #^ and the name: [[#^ask-sam]].

lessons.title: A board
lessons.teach: A block marked board lays named items out as columns. Each line of it is a column: its name, a colon, and the names of the items in it. The items stay in the note as they were, and dragging a card to another column moves it there.
lessons.example:
```board
To do: ship-page
Done: pick-date
```

- [ ] Ship the pricing page ^ship-page
- [x] Pick a launch date ^pick-date
lessons.task: Make a board with a column or two.
lessons.hint: Three backticks and board, a line like To do: ship-page, then three backticks, and an item named ^ship-page.

lessons.title: A board’s height
lessons.teach: Left to itself a board is as tall as its longest column. Drag the line under it to set a height, and the columns scroll inside it; the height is written on the fence as height=, in the board’s own text size. A double tap on the line takes it off again.
lessons.example:
```board height=12
To do: ship-page
Done: pick-date
```

- [ ] Ship the pricing page ^ship-page
- [x] Pick a launch date ^pick-date
lessons.task: Give a board a height of its own.
lessons.hint: After the word board on the first line, a space and height= with a number: ```board height=12.

lessons.title: A ticket
lessons.teach: A note whose front matter says type: ticket is a ticket. Its status, who it is for, its priority and its due day sit under that line, and are drawn as a card you tap to change. A notebook with a ticket key numbers its tickets, and [[GHO-12]] links to one by its key.
lessons.example:
---
type: ticket
id: GHO-12
status: In progress
assignee: Sam
---
# Fix the login loop
lessons.task: Make a note a ticket, with a status.
lessons.hint: At the very top: three dashes, type: ticket, status: To do, then three dashes again.

lessons.title: A ticket notebook
lessons.teach: A notebook whose front matter has a key numbers the tickets made in it: key: GLY gives GLY-1, then GLY-2 and on. Make this a ticket, under More on the +, turns the note you are in into its notebook’s next ticket.
lessons.task: Make a notebook with a ticket key.
lessons.praise: Its tickets will be numbered by that key.
lessons.hint: At the very top: three dashes, book: true, key: and two to five capital letters, then three dashes again.

lessons.title: A query
lessons.teach: A fence called query lists what matches across every note: to-dos, tickets or notes. Say where from, what has to be true, and how to show it, a line each, and it is drawn as a list, a table, a board, a month or a timeline that keeps up as your notes change. More › A database, on the + beside an empty line, writes a ready-made one.
lessons.example:
```query
from: tasks
where: due <= today+7
show: list
```
lessons.task: Write a query that lists your open to-dos.
lessons.praise: Every open to-do, in one place.
lessons.hint: Three backticks and query, then from: tasks on the next line, then three backticks to close it.

lessons.title: Narrow it down
lessons.teach: where: keeps only what is true: status != Done, due < today, priority >= high, assignee = Sam, joined with and or or. sort: puts what is left in order, by one field or several.
lessons.example:
```query
from: tickets
where: status != Done and priority >= high
sort: due
```
lessons.task: Write a query with a where: line.
lessons.hint: Inside a query fence, a line like where: status != Done.

lessons.title: Show it another way
lessons.teach: show: draws the same answer as a table, a list, a board, a calendar month, a gantt timeline or a count. A query drawn as a board keeps a height as a board does: drag the line under it.
lessons.task: Show a query as a board, a table, a calendar or a timeline.
lessons.praise: The same answer, drawn another way.
lessons.hint: Inside a query fence, a line like show: board, or show: calendar.

lessons.title: Group and add up
lessons.teach: group: gives each value of one field its own heading, or its own lane on a board. total: adds a number up, under each group and at the end: an estimate, or any field of your own.
lessons.example:
```query
from: tickets
group: assignee
total: estimate
show: table
```
lessons.task: Group a query, or add something up.
lessons.hint: Inside a query fence, a line like group: status, or total: estimate.

lessons.title: A spoiler
lessons.teach: Two bars either side turn the words to smoke until the caret is in them: the end of a film, a surprise.
lessons.task: Keep a secret in a line.
lessons.hint: Two bars either side: ||like this||.

lessons.title: A highlight
lessons.teach: Two equals signs either side put a wash of color behind the words, for the line you will want again.
lessons.task: Highlight something.
lessons.hint: Two equals signs either side: ==like this==.

lessons.title: A colored highlight
lessons.teach: A color’s name in brackets straight after a highlight changes its color: blue, red, amber, green, teal, purple or gray.
lessons.task: Highlight something in a color.
lessons.hint: A highlight, then the color in brackets with no space: ==this==(green).

lessons.title: An aside
lessons.teach: Two percent signs either side make a note to yourself inside the note: smaller, quieter, leaning.
lessons.example: the train at nine %%or the one after%%
lessons.task: Write an aside.
lessons.hint: Two percent signs either side: %%like this%%.

lessons.title: Unsure
lessons.teach: Two question marks either side draw a dotted line under a fact to check later.
lessons.task: Mark something you are not sure of.
lessons.hint: Two question marks either side: ??like this??.

lessons.title: A note on a mark
lessons.teach: Words in brackets straight after a mark are a note on it, and a tap on the words in a note shows it. On a fact you are unsure of, it says why.
lessons.task: Put a note on a mark.
lessons.praise: That is a note on the mark: tap the words to read it.
lessons.hint: A mark, then the note in brackets with no space: ??four hundred??(why).

lessons.title: A redaction
lessons.teach: Two at signs either side put a solid bar of ink over the words. It lifts while the caret is in them, so they can still be read and edited, and a share still has the words.
lessons.example: the name on the lease is @@Sam Ortiz@@
lessons.task: Put a bar over something.
lessons.hint: Two at signs either side: @@like this@@.

lessons.title: A shout
lessons.teach: Two carets either side set the words in spaced small capitals: emphasis that is not bold.
lessons.task: Shout something.
lessons.hint: Two carets either side: ^^like this^^.

lessons.title: Added
lessons.teach: Two plus signs either side underline what was added, the partner of struck through for what went.
lessons.task: Mark something as added.
lessons.hint: Two plus signs either side: ++like this++.

lessons.title: Heat
lessons.teach: Two flames either side make the words bold, and the line above them wavers in the heat coming off them. An effect lifts while the caret is in its words, so they edit as plain text.
lessons.example:
The air above wavers
🔥🔥too hot to touch🔥🔥
lessons.task: Heat some words, with a line above them.
lessons.hint: Two flames either side: 🔥🔥like this🔥🔥. One flame is only a flame.

lessons.title: Frost
lessons.teach: Two snowflakes either side turn the words cold, a rime creeping over their edges and settling.
lessons.task: Freeze some words.
lessons.hint: Two snowflakes either side: ❄️❄️like this❄️❄️.

lessons.title: A wave
lessons.teach: Two waves either side set the words bobbing along the line, a ripple passing through them.
lessons.task: Send some words out on a wave.
lessons.hint: Two waves either side: 🌊🌊like this🌊🌊.

lessons.title: A shimmer
lessons.teach: Two sparkles either side send a glint across the words every few seconds.
lessons.task: Make some words shimmer.
lessons.hint: Two sparkles either side: ✨✨like this✨✨.

lessons.title: A haunting
lessons.teach: Two ghosts either side make the words fade almost away and back, slowly, like something passing.
lessons.task: Haunt some words.
lessons.hint: Two ghosts either side: 👻👻like this👻👻.
